title: Microstructure-informed constitutive modeling of granular media under multidirectional loading: From particle-scale to continuum
task: Develop microstructure-informed constitutive model for granular media under multidirectional loading using DEM and deep learning
key_results: Deep-learning model trained on DEM simulations captures particle-scale kinematics and contact forces; predicts granular response under complex loading paths with direct application to wind turbine foundation optimization
comments: Bridges particle simulation and continuum prediction effectively, though generalization to field-scale heterogeneous soils and validation against in-situ measurements remain open.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Deep-learning models replicate complex nonlinear DEM relationships for granular media
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; approach addresses computational intensity and enables engineering optimization

title: STRAIGHT-IN Dual: a platform for dual single-copy integrations of DNA payloads and gene circuits into human induced pluripotent stem cells
task: Enable efficient dual single-copy DNA integration into hiPSCs for testing gene circuits and cell programming
key_results: Simultaneous allele-specific single-copy integration of two constructs achieved in 1 week; demonstrated control of transgene silencing and tunable/temporally controlled expression via dual inducible switches (tetracycline and grazoprevir-inducible systems)
comments: STRAIGHT-IN Dual substantially accelerates design-build-test cycles by achieving scarless, component-recyclable integrations, though long-term transgene stability and off-target effects in hiPSCs warrant further investigation.

hypotheses.hypothesis: Promoter choice and gene syntax influence transgene silencing and reporter expression

hypotheses.hypothesis: Dual inducible switches (tetracycline and grazoprevir) enable independent, tunable control of different transcription factors
hypotheses.result: Confirmed; temporal control of heterologous transcription factors achieved within same cell

title: Probing the diversity in dairy cattle reticulorumen temperature for adaptation selection
task: Identify variability in thermal stress response for heat-tolerance selection in dairy cattle
key_results: Reticulorumen temperature deviation shows positive association with THI; significant inter-individual variability in thermal sensitivity; THI threshold of 65 identified as critical point for physiological response
comments: Phenotypic characterization is valuable, but mechanistic understanding of individual thermal tolerance and its genetic basis remain unclear from this descriptive analysis.

hypotheses.result: Confirmed with significant inter-individual variability; THI threshold of 65 identified as critical

hypotheses.hypothesis: Baseline THI levels influence downstream thermal response
